results.summary: This project is a 4x4 array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit inputs m and q to produce an 8-bit product p. It was created using manual structural design with AND gates and full adders. The full adder module takes three 1-bit inputs and produces a 1-bit sum and carry out. The design generates four 4-bit partial products and sums them to produce the final output.

results.summary_before: This project is a 16-bit experimental CPU called GUS16 with a serial port, PWM output, general purpose I/O and an external memory interface, with memory provided off-chip. It includes a bootloader that loads programs over the serial port, and the documented basic test is to connect at 115200 baud, 8N1, and send an 'L', which should be echoed back. More complete testing requires an external board with SRAM and address latches attached to the user PMOD connectors, and that memory board is noted as still pending design. The design is documented in an accompanying PDF and occupies a 1x2 tile area.
results.summary: This project is a 4-bit multiplier that takes two 4-bit integers and outputs a single 8-bit integer. It was created using manual structural design with AND gates and 1-bit full adders. The partial products are aligned diagonally to mimic manual binary multiplication. The project was created for NYU's digital logic course Lab 4.

results.summary: This project implements a 16-bit noise-shaping delta-sigma DAC with a single digital output pin. It uses a pulse width modulator to create the digital output signal. The design can be driven with sample data or a built-in triangle wave generator for testing. The output can be low-pass filtered and converted to audio using an external audio Pmod.
